questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Chile?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Chile article.

questions.proof: The center of Chile, with the two cities Santiago and Valparaíso, has a Mediterranean climate with an average temperature of 28 °C (82 °F) in January and 11 °C (52 °F) in July.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Chile?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Chile article.

questions.proof: Chile's currency is the Chilean peso.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Chile about 756,102 square kilometres; Norway about 385,207 square kilometres; Guyana about 214,970 square kilometres; Panama about 74,177 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Santiago?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Chile is Santiago.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Chile?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Chile on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Chile article.

questions.proof: Chile borders Peru to the north, Bolivia to the northeast, Argentina to the east, and the Drake Passage in the far south.
